summary: C trap.c:animate_statue removes a worn statue before deleting it. JS recorded that call as unported, leaving a wielded statue in the weapon slot after stone-to-flesh animation. The fix calls the existing steal.js remove_worn_item implementation before delobj; the admitted case now matches completely.

source.branch: When a statue has a nonzero owornmask, animate_statue calls remove_worn_item(statue, TRUE) after monster inventory setup and before delobj.
callers: zap.c:stone_to_flesh_obj calls animate_statue with ANIMATE_SPELL for a statue hit by stone-to-flesh; this is the admitted mismatch path.
trap.c:activate_statue_trap calls animate_statue for a triggered statue trap.

evidence: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:888-889: animate_statue removes a worn statue before deleting it. The same function is called by zap.c:stone_to_flesh_obj and trap.c:activate_statue_trap.

At the examined commit, js/trap.js:3532-3534 called note_unported('steal.c remove_worn_item') before delobj. The existing js/steal.js:330-374 implementation clears W_WEAPONS state through uwepgone and setnotworn.
